_authority: What a course-facing page may SAY. Read by scripts/check_slide_text.py. Edit this file, not the script.
_why: A maritime subject-matter reviewer read a finished module and returned four rules. None of them is about any one course: each is about the difference between a document the Training Centre keeps for itself and a page a trainee reads. Internal shorthand, internal version control, and a training-requirement document cited as if it were a technical reference all make a course look like an internal working file instead of teaching material - and the last one is worse than untidy, because it tells a trainee that a syllabus is a source of fact.

surfaces._what: Which pages these rules bite on. A rule that fires everywhere would flag an instructor's own planning notes, where citing a training requirement is exactly right.
surfaces._presentation_note: Everything a TRAINEE sees, plus the deck an instructor drives in front of them. The rules are enforced here.
surfaces._instructor_note: An instructor's plan, run sheet or analysis. Citing a training requirement HERE is legitimate and useful - it is how an instructor knows why a topic is in the course. Reported as a note, never a failure.

internal_abbreviations._what: Shorthand used inside the Training Centre. It is not an IMO title, not an international standard and not an industry abbreviation, and printing it on a slide implies all three. Write the course out in full instead.
internal_abbreviations._add_one: Add {term, instead, why}. The term is matched as a whole word, case-insensitively.

terms.instead: Basic Training for Oil and Chemical Tanker Cargo Operations (Familiarization)
terms.why: an internal Training Centre abbreviation; it is not an IMO or industry term

never_cite_as_source._what: Documents that govern what a course must COVER, and are not references for what a course TEACHES.
never_cite_as_source._why: An IMO model course is a training requirement and a guideline for course content. It is not a source of factual information, and a slide that says 'Source: IMO Model Course 1.01' tells the room that a syllabus is where the fact came from. Cite the publication the fact actually came from - the books, codes and documents in the source files - or cite nothing.
never_cite_as_source._figures_too: This includes figure and diagram attributions: 'Figure: IMO Model Course 1.01, 1.2'. Do not redraw a model-course figure and credit the model course; credit the publication the model course itself drew on, or leave the figure uncredited.

patterns.label: an IMO model course
patterns.why: a training requirement, not a source of fact

patterns.label: a model course by number
patterns.why: a training requirement, not a source of fact

no_version_control_on_slides._what: Revision numbers, approval status and internal programme designations.
no_version_control_on_slides._why: A title slide is the first thing a room sees. It should look like training material, not like an internal version-control record. The programme's approval is real and belongs in the course plan and the companion file - not on the screen in front of trainees.
no_version_control_on_slides._hardest_on: the opening slide, where it fails; elsewhere on a slide it is a warning
no_version_control_on_slides._title_only_note: Some of these are only wrong as a STAMP. 'The approved programme allows a maximum of 24 trainees' is useful prose in a handout; 'Approved LJA programme, revision 3' on a title slide is a version-control record. Patterns marked title_only fail on the opening slide and are ignored in body text; the rest - a revision number, an internal authority designation - are wrong anywhere a trainee reads them.

honesty_markers._what: The factory's own markers for work that is not finished or not ratified.
honesty_markers._why: They are a message from the build to the owner, and they belong in factory-notes.md where the owner reads them. On a slide they are noise to a trainee and an admission of doubt in front of a class. The companion file already exists for exactly this - no second file is needed.
honesty_markers._unknown_note: UNKNOWN is deliberately NOT listed: it is an ordinary English word that appears in real teaching text ('the cargo is unknown'). The marker form is caught by the others.
